channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Harlow police want to speak to Damien Clinton, 33, over theft inquiry
item.description: Officers say he has connections to Harlow and tattoos on the backs of his hands.

item.title: Colchester police seek Gavyn Booker, 34, wanted on recall to prison
item.description: He has long brown hair and a beard, and has connections to Colchester.

item.title: Police hunt Connor Downer, 22, wanted on recall to prison
item.description: Essex Police say he has links to Colchester, Ipswich and the Tendring district.

item.title: Child, 11, bitten by dog at Basildon recreation ground
item.description: Police want to trace the man walking what is believed to be a German Shepherd puppy at Markhams Chase Recreation Ground.

item.title: Harlow police want to speak to Damien Clinton, 33, in theft inquiry
item.description: Essex Police are asking the public to help find a 33-year-old man with links to Harlow.

item.title: Stansted Airport College welcomes Kemi Badenoch for student talks
item.description: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, MP for North West Essex, visited Stansted Airport College to see how its students move from training into work.

item.title: Southend Pier trains: calls grow for a firm date to restart £3.5m railway
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council is under growing pressure to set a firm date for the pier's £3.5m trains to run again, the Yellow Advertiser reports.

item.title: Colchester Leisure World swimming pool shut for cleaning after incident
item.description: Colchester Leisure World closed its main pool on Friday 20 November for cleaning after an incident, cancelling some swimming lessons, while its Aqua Springs spa stayed open, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: One of Essex Police's first female detective sergeants retires after 48 years
item.description: Deirdre Nowell joined the force in 1978, when a woman officer's uniform came with a handbag and an allowance for tights.

item.title: Dedham bridge once saw 90,000+ turkeys walked to London for Christmas
item.description: Turkeys reared in East Anglia were once driven for about three months through Essex to Smithfield Market in London in time for Christmas, BBC News reports.

item.title: Chelmsford police urgently search for Johnny Coyle, 37, who may be hurt
item.description: Anyone who sees him should not approach him but call 999, quoting incident 892 of 20 November.

item.title: Harlow Market Square's first rebuild phase is finished
item.description: The square in Harlow town centre now has water jets, granite paving, rain gardens, seating, lighting and CCTV, Your Harlow reports.

item.title: Colchester United go to Tranmere looking to build on Gillingham win
item.description: Danny Cowley's U's sit just three points above the League Two drop zone, but he has never lost to Tranmere Rovers since taking charge in Colchester.

item.title: Essex football fixtures: Colchester go to Tranmere on Saturday
item.description: Three Isthmian North Division games are all-Essex derbies, while Billericay Town and Chelmsford City face the two bottom clubs in the National League South.

item.title: Dengie solar farm: wider public consultation planned for early 2027
item.description: Residents across the Dengie Peninsula will get a fuller say on Low Carbon's seven-site, 4,200-acre plan before the firm applies to the government for consent.

item.title: Benfleet student builds life-size Dalek for his degree
item.description: Ben Dobinson, 27, from Benfleet, spent more than 300 hours on the Doctor Who villain for his modelmaking course, BBC News reports.

item.title: Boxted Bridge on Essex-Suffolk border still shut after three years
item.description: Politicians on both sides of the Stour are calling for urgent action to reopen Boxted Bridge, near Colchester, the East Anglian Daily Times reports.

item.title: Maldon Salt labelling questions passed to Essex Trading Standards
item.description: Maldon District Council says it has no concerns about Maldon Salt's sites, the Maldon Standard reports, after an Observer investigation found the firm mixes German rock salt into its sea salt.

item.title: Shrimpers lose five-goal table-top thriller
item.description: Tyreece Simpson and debutant Rico Richards struck two minutes apart after the break, but the Shrimpers could not complete the comeback against the runaway leaders.

item.title: Southend seafront road gets almost 5,000 parking fines in a year
item.description: The penalty charge notices were all issued on a single road on Southend-on-Sea's seafront over 12 months, the Yellow Advertiser reports.

item.title: Basildon council pledges to revive town centre as shops close
item.description: Basildon's council has promised to rejuvenate the town centre after residents said its shops keep shutting down, the Yellow Advertiser reports.

item.title: Police appeal to find Basildon man, 49, not heard from for weeks
item.description: Officers are worried about Valeriy Hurynchuk and say he may be using a white Skoda Fabia.

item.title: Greater Anglia trains to Stansted Airport hit by signalling failure
item.description: A signalling fault caused hours of disruption for Greater Anglia passengers travelling to and from Stansted Airport on the evening of Friday 20 November, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: RAF Wethersfield dispersal order in force until midnight on Monday
item.description: Essex Police say the order around the former airbase near Braintree keeps emergency access to the site open while allowing lawful protest.

item.title: Westcliff's Hamlet Court Road gets Christmas lights after community push
item.description: People in Westcliff, Southend, rallied round to make a Christmas lights switch-on happen in the road often called the city's second high street, the Echo reports.

item.title: A127 drivers face months of lane and slip road closures
item.description: Maintenance, resurfacing and utility works will bring lane and slip road closures along the A127 in south Essex from Monday 23 November into January 2027, the Echo reports.

item.title: Brentwood School coach Gareth Stafford Bull likely abused pupils, review finds
item.description: The school's own independent review says the fencing coach probably harmed a number of boys through the 1980s and 1990s, and that former pupils who came forward years later were brushed off. British Fencing is now launching its own inquiry.

item.title: Chelmsford's New Hall School wins national ISA award for sport
item.description: The Boreham school, led by head Katherine Jeffrey, beat other large independent schools to the Independent Schools Association prize.

item.title: Great Clacton church hall to be demolished and rebuilt after approval
item.description: Tendring District Council has approved plans to replace the ageing hall at the Grade I-listed St John the Baptist Church in Great Clacton, the Clacton and Frinton Gazette reports.

item.title: Billericay High Street gets Alice in Wonderland-themed tea room
item.description: The Enchanted Cottage tea room, serving cakes, afternoon tea and cream teas, opens in Billericay on Saturday 21 November, the Echo reports.

item.title: Braintree Village ice rink holds inclusive skate for disability groups
item.description: More than 90 guests from disability groups took to the ice in Braintree at a session set aside for them, the Braintree & Witham Times reports.

item.title: Clacton primary school's garden in running for county award
item.description: A school garden project in Clacton-on-Sea is among the finalists for Essex School Garden of the Year, the Clacton Gazette reports.

item.title: Essex's 5,200 charities and community groups add £4.6bn, audit finds
item.description: Essex Community Foundation has published its Community Listening Project audit of the county's voluntary, community and social enterprise sector, looking at funding, staff and volunteer pressures.

item.title: Braintree council sets out first budget plans for 2027-28
item.description: Braintree District Council has published its initial budget proposals for 2027-28, saying they are designed to protect services and support residents across the district.

item.title: Clacton's former ATS Euromaster garage goes up for sale
item.description: The ATS Euromaster site in Clacton has been put up for sale after the tyre and car servicing chain stopped trading in the UK, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Broomfield Hospital gets £4.3m nuclear medicine suite for cancer scans
item.description: Two new scanners at the Chelmsford hospital will help doctors find and track cancer, Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust says.

item.title: Essex weekend travel: buses replace trains from Colchester on Sunday
item.description: Rail passengers on the main line and the Braintree branch face replacement buses, and the QEII Bridge at the Dartford Crossing shuts overnight on Saturday 21 November.

item.title: Essex opticians treat new eye problems without a GP visit, NHS Essex says
item.description: The free Minor Eye Conditions Service runs at participating opticians across the county and can save patients a trip to A&E.

item.title: Maldon's Promenade Park gets free outdoor gym as work begins
item.description: Maldon District Council said on Friday 20 November that building has started on a new outdoor gym at Promenade Park in Maldon, free for visitors to use.

item.title: Essex anti-social behaviour reports up 76% as robbery falls 19%
item.description: The Seax analysis of police.uk data shows anti-social behaviour reports rose in 50 of Essex Police's 56 neighbourhood areas in September 2026 compared with September 2025, with Basildon recording the most.

item.title: Tendring offers £100,000+ in health grants to sport and community groups
item.description: Clubs and groups across the Tendring district can bid for money for projects that get people active, eating well or looking after their mental health.

item.title: NHS Essex looks for new online consultation tools for 204 GP surgeries
item.description: Suppliers can show their systems at an online event on 9 December, and a two-year contract is due to start in spring 2027.

item.title: Two taken to hospital after A282 crash shuts QEII Bridge for hours
item.description: Both were taken by road to the Royal London Hospital, and more closures are planned at the Dartford Crossing tonight and on Saturday.

item.title: Three Colchester food outlets hold hygiene ratings of 0 or 1
item.description: A High Street restaurant has the lowest rating, zero, and two other city centre businesses are rated one after inspections in October, an analysis of Food Standards Agency data by The Seax shows.

item.title: Grays and Tilbury town boards replaced by councillor working groups
item.description: Thurrock Council's cabinet has agreed the change as regeneration projects in the two towns move from planning into delivery, Your Thurrock reports.

item.title: Grays school trust plans indoor padel courts on Green Belt site
item.description: South West Essex Community Education Trust wants to build a sports hall with two padel courts at William Edwards School in Grays, open to public bookings in the evenings.

item.title: Thurrock Council's Inspire careers team up for national inclusion award
item.description: Thurrock Council's Inspire Employability and Skills team is shortlisted for Inclusive Team of the Year at the Inspiring Women in Local Government Awards 2026.

item.title: Colchester Castle roof repairs finished after £1.3m project
item.description: Colchester City Council says work to stop water getting into the Norman keep has been completed.

item.title: 19-year-old Harlow man charged over hospital & McDonald's trespass
item.description: A Harlow man has been charged with entering a staff room at the town's hospital and an area of a McDonald's restaurant as a trespasser with intent to steal, Your Harlow reports.

item.title: Clacton Hospital's £25m revamp brings new urgent care centre
item.description: Children's services and musculoskeletal therapy have also moved into the rebuilt space, with Tendring council paying £2m of the cost.

item.title: Stansted Airport plans major emergency exercise with 400 taking part
item.description: London Stansted will rehearse its response to an aircraft accident using a decommissioned plane, and the airport says flights should not be affected.

item.title: Harlow's Avant Garde salon on The Rows shuts without warning
item.description: Clients of the long-running Harlow town centre hair and beauty salon found its doors shut this week.

item.title: Leigh phone mast on London Road to rise to 20 metres despite objections
item.description: Southend City Council has decided no further action is needed on Three's plan for a taller mast at 954 London Road, Leigh-on-Sea, near Iceland, Your Southend reports.

item.title: Harlow to switch on bigger Christmas lights display on Broad Walk
item.description: Harlow Council says this year's town centre display is bigger and brighter than before, with lights across more of the town.

item.title: Danbury man, 79, fined for racially abusing Stansted Airport security
item.description: Magistrates in Chelmsford found William Ryan guilty of two counts of racially aggravated harassment after he abused staff at a London Stansted security scanner.

item.title: Basildon neighbour rescues sleeping woman after hearing smoke alarm
item.description: A woman who fell asleep while food was in the oven was helped out of her Basildon maisonette by a neighbour on 19 November.

item.title: Basildon councillors back permanent war memorial D-Day veteran sought
item.description: Basildon and Laindon have no permanent war memorial. Basildon Council has now voted unanimously to change that, taking up Don Sheppard's long campaign.

item.title: Colchester Hospital asks patients to hand back crutches and frames
item.description: The north Essex hospital trust cleans, checks and repairs returned walking aids so they can go to other patients.

item.title: Tendring plans to backdate council tax support for working-age claimants
item.description: Tendring District Council wants to extend a rule that now helps only pension-age claimants. Other council tax discounts and premiums in the district stay the same in 2027/28.

item.title: Tendring council runs £3.9m under budget at half-year, mainly on timing
item.description: Tendring District Council says the gap mainly reflects when money is spent and received across several budgets.
